title: El recibo de la luz en la colonia Roma

dialogue.speaker: Mateo
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Lucía, no te pases... Acabo de ver el recibo de la luz de este bimestre y casi me da un infarto.
dialogue.english: Hey, Lucía, come on now... I just saw this two-month electricity bill and I almost had a heart attack.

slang.actualMeaning: come on / don't go too far / you're kidding me
slang.example: ¡No te pases, te comiste todo el pastel!

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Aguanta, Mateo, no te esponjes. Es que la semana pasada hizo un frío horrible y dejé el calentador eléctrico prendido un par de noches.
dialogue.english: Hold on, Mateo, don't get worked up. Last week it was freezing cold and I left the electric space heater on for a couple of nights.

slang.actualMeaning: don't get puffed up / don't get worked up or angry
slang.example: Tranquilo, no te esponjes, fue solo una broma.

dialogue.speaker: Mateo
dialogue.spanish: ¿Un par de noches? ¡Pero si subió al doble! Y tú sabes que ahorita ando bien bruja porque no me han pagado el proyecto de diseño.
dialogue.english: A couple of nights? It doubled! And you know I'm super broke right now because they haven't paid me for the design project yet.

slang.actualMeaning: completely broke / out of money (andar bruja)
slang.example: Fin de quincena y ya ando bien bruja.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Tranquilo, mi primo Javi me debía una lana de los boletos del concierto y me acaba de transferir. Yo pongo el setenta por ciento del recibo.
dialogue.english: Relax, my cousin Javi owed me cash for the concert tickets and he just sent me a transfer. I'll cover seventy percent of the bill.

dialogue.speaker: Mateo
dialogue.spanish: Uf, qué alivio... Es que el casero ya me estaba moliendo por WhatsApp desde las ocho de la mañana.
dialogue.english: Phew, what a relief... The landlord was already nagging me on WhatsApp since eight in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Ya sé cómo se pone. Ándale, yo lo pago ahorita en la app y además te invito unos esquites si me echas la mano con las cajas de la bodega.
dialogue.english: I know how he gets. Come on, I'll pay it right now in the app and treat you to some corn cups too if you give me a hand with the storage room boxes.

slang.actualMeaning: lend a hand / help someone out (echar la mano)
slang.example: ¿Me echas la mano para subir este sillón?

questions.question: What caused the two-month electricity bill in Mateo and Lucía's apartment to double?
options: Lucía left the electric space heater on for a couple of freezing nights last week
Mateo left his computer running day and night
The landlord billed them for the whole building
questions.explanation: Lucía admits she left the electric space heater on ('dejé el calentador eléctrico prendido un par de noches').

questions.question: Why is Mateo broke right now, and how much of the bill does Lucía agree to cover?
options: He hasn't been paid for his design project yet; Lucía covers 70% of the bill
He bought concert tickets; Lucía covers 50% of the bill
He lost his wallet; Lucía covers 100% of the bill
He paid the water bill; Lucía covers 30% of the bill
questions.explanation: Mateo hasn't been paid for his design project yet, and Lucía covers 70% after her cousin Javi paid her back.

questions.question: What favor does Lucía ask of Mateo in exchange for treating him to 'esquites'?
options: Help her with the boxes in the storage room ('la bodega')
Walk her dog in the park
questions.explanation: Lucía says: 'te invito unos esquites si me echas la mano con las cajas de la bodega.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: What do 'no te esponjes', 'andar bruja', and 'echar la mano' mean in Mexican Spanish?
options: 'No te esponjes' = don't get worked up; 'andar bruja' = to be broke; 'echar la mano' = to lend a hand
'No te esponjes' = don't get wet; 'andar bruja' = to stay up late; 'echar la mano' = to wave goodbye
'No te esponjes' = don't eat too much; 'andar bruja' = to be angry; 'echar la mano' = to applaud
'No te esponjes' = don't fall asleep; 'andar bruja' = to be lucky; 'echar la mano' = to pay in cash
questions.explanation: 'No te esponjes' means don't get puffed up/angry, 'andar bruja' means to be broke, and 'echar la mano' means to lend a hand!
